newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures slip late, most end down.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures slip late, most end down.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended mostly lower, faltering late amid thin trading.

September Standard & Poor's 500 futures fell from tentative gains to end just above session lows. Traders said thin trading had turned the pit illiquid, exacerbating late local selling to drag September lower.
They estimated September S&P 500 volume at a light 49,000 contracts. Trade was very thin after T-bond futures closed, traders said.
Earlier in the session trade was more lively, and September hit a fresh record high at 912.40.
Traders said that expiration-related buying helped keep the market buoyant earlier.
June S&P 500 futures expired on Thursday's close and settled early Friday. Traders said June's unofficial settlement price was 898.65, up slightly from Thursday's close.
Also expiring at week's end are individual equity options, S&P 500 index options and S&P 100 index options.
But by the last hour of trade, expiration-related activity had faded, traders said.

"It looked like a pretty good sell-off, but there's not much out here," an S&P 500 futures trader said. As for expiration activity, "overall I'd say it was non-event," he said, adding that traders had been positioning for expiration over the last two days.
Another trader said locals were featured sellers just before the close, along with scattered selling from a dealer or two.
Overall, they said the afternoon was unremarkable.
Resistance now stands at 913.00 and 912.40, with support at the 904.00 session low and 902.50, traders said.

At the close, September S&P 500 futures were down 2.65 points to 904.85, Nasdaq 100s were 8.00 lower at 989.00, Russell 2000s were down 1.50 points to 399.35, KCBT Value Line futures fell 4.20 points to 794.95, Nikkei 225 index futures fell 75.0 to 20,530.0 and Midcap 400s fell 0.80 point to 293.10.
